subject: silver carp
title: On These Rivers, a Boat Motor Makes 110-Pound Fish Fly 10 Feet

scenes.text: On some American rivers, the danger isn't in the water. It's flying out of it.
Silver carp can leap up to ten feet into the air.
The trigger is the sound of an outboard motor.
They grow to 110 pounds and nearly four feet long. Now picture one hitting you at boat speed.
They've seriously injured many boaters. Water skiing on parts of the Missouri River is called exceedingly dangerous.
They came from Asia and now fill much of the Mississippi basin. The boat isn't the danger. It's what it wakes up.

description:
Invasive silver carp leap as high as 10 feet out of the water when startled, especially by outboard motors.
They can reach 110 pounds and nearly 4 feet long, and the USGS says jumping fish have seriously injured many boaters and damaged boats. Originally from Asia, they are now established through much of the Mississippi River basin.
Would you still go boating on these rivers?
first_comment: Passing trains, geese taking off and even rocks thrown into the water can set them off too. Would you risk a boat ride?
